notes: Read the full 202-line source hook line by line before editing. The web hook is entirely browser-only: html2canvas-pro rasterization, document.createElement('a') anchor downloads, URL.createObjectURL, navigator.clipboard + ClipboardItem, XMLSerializer, and canvas.toBlob/toDataURL — none of which exist in React Native. Per contract rule 7 this is ported as a native-safe implementation with explicit unavailable state documented here.

Imports (web L1): kept useCallback/useRef/useState from react and added the MutableRefObject type; replaced the DOM HTMLDivElement ref type with a React Native View ref (import type {View} from 'react-native'). No DOM modules, browser HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, html2canvas, or old web UI components are imported.

JSDoc header (web L3-41): rewritten for native while preserving every documented behaviour — capture target wiring (web L9-15), SVG export semantics (web L17-24), the three ClipboardOutcome cases (web L26-35), and the prefers-reduced-motion note (web L37-40). Added an explicit native-divergence summary naming the missing browser primitives.

CAPTURE_BACKGROUND '#0a0a0f' (web L43): preserved verbatim and still used — threaded into NATIVE_CAPTURE_OPTIONS.backgroundColor (the config a future capture adapter receives), mirroring web L70 html2canvas backgroundColor.

ClipboardOutcome type (web L45): ported verbatim. ChartExportApi interface (web L47-55): ported field-for-field with identical JSDoc; only chartRef's element type changed from HTMLDivElement to the native View (ChartCaptureTarget alias). exportPNG/exportSVG/copyToClipboard signatures and the exporting boolean are unchanged.

makeFilename (web L57-65): ported verbatim — same sanitize regexes ([^a-z0-9-_]+ -> '-', trim leading/trailing '-'), same 'chart' fallback, same ISO date slice(0,10), same `${safe}-${date}.${ext}` shape. Exercised by all three export paths.

Browser capture/IO helpers replaced with documented native-safe seams: snapshotToCanvas/html2canvas (web L67-75) -> snapshotChart() typed Promise<NativeChartImage> that throws ChartExportUnavailableError; downloadHref/downloadBlob anchor+createObjectURL (web L77-95) -> downloadChartText() that throws the same error; serializeFirstChildSVG XMLSerializer/querySelector (web L97-108) -> serializeChartSvg() returning null (no DOM <svg> on native, matching web's no-svg branch); canvasToBlob (web L110-114) folded into snapshotChart unavailability; getClipboardItemCtor/window.ClipboardItem (web L116-119) removed — clipboard image API absence captured by nativeChartExportCapabilities.clipboardImageAvailable=false. Added nativeChartExportCapabilities + ChartExportUnavailableError (mirrors the existing useSettingsBackup.ts unavailable pattern).

useChartExport hook (web L121-202): preserved exactly — chartRef via useRef<View|null>(null) (web L122), exporting useState (web L123), and the three useCallback exporters with identical [filename, exporting] deps and identical guards (!chartRef.current || exporting). exportPNG (web L125-136) and exportSVG (web L138-161, including the quiet no-svg console.warn bail) keep the setExporting true/try/catch-log/finally-false flow. copyToClipboard (web L163-199) preserves the 'copied'/'fallback'/'failed' union and snapshot-first ordering, mapping the native no-rasterizer case to web's 'failed' (snapshot failed) branch; 'copied'/'fallback' are reserved for a future react-native-view-shot + Share/Clipboard adapter. Return shape {chartRef, exporting, exportPNG, exportSVG, copyToClipboard} is identical (web L201). No i18n or unit conversion exists in the source, so none was introduced.

Verification: from apps/native ran npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit), npm run lint -- --quiet (eslint), and npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles (jest) — all pass. Public API matches the existing native consumer components/charts/ChartExportMenu.tsx (onExportPNG/onExportSVG/onCopyImage + ClipboardOutcome).
